quizzes.title: Sanctions and Strategic Interests
quizzes.passage: Venezuela has been at the centre of a sharp dispute with Washington. After Juan Guaido declared himself Acting President, tensions with Washington rose further. Caracas reacted sharply to these developments. The United States then imposed sanctions on the state-owned oil firm, which is central to the country's economy. Venezuela holds some of the largest oil reserves in the world, so the dispute has a strong energy dimension. Venezuela has also built relationships with several governments outside the region, and Washington has watched these ties closely. Caracas has rejected the allegations made against it, arguing that they are used to justify a change of government. Caracas also says that migration and drug issues are being used as a cover for political goals. Economic pressure has become a central feature of the dispute, shaping how both governments describe their goals and the steps they take next. Venezuela's economy has suffered deep problems in recent years, including high inflation and power outages. Shortages of food and problems in healthcare have added to the strain on ordinary citizens. Nicolas Maduro has led the government through these years, and critics have questioned the fairness of recent elections. Caracas and Washington give very different accounts of the dispute and its causes.

questions.q: According to the booklet, the sanctions on the state-owned oil firm aimed to cut Maduro's access to which source of income?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the sanctions aimed to cut off Maduro's access to oil revenue, Venezuela's primary income source.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Venezuela's partnerships with China, Russia, Iran and Cuba cover energy, defence and finance.
Reason (R): The US views these alignments as a challenge to its strategic dominance in the Western Hemisphere.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the US view of these alignments does not explain what the partnerships cover.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Maduro's retaliation for US recognition of Guaido   ->   A. Severed diplomatic ties and expelled American diplomats
II. US response after sanctions failed to dislodge Maduro   ->   B. Maritime interdictions aimed at choking oil revenues
III. Preferred style of US diplomacy   ->   C. Unilateral and transactional diplomacy over multilateralism
IV. Legal banner for US maritime actions   ->   D. Counter-narcotics operations and national security enforcement
questions.explanation: Maduro severed ties in retaliation, the US turned to maritime interdictions after sanctions failed, and the booklet pairs US policy with unilateral diplomacy and a counter-narcotics framing.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the US-Venezuela dispute:
I. Sections of Venezuela's domestic opposition have endorsed stronger external pressure.
II. Venezuela's partnerships with China, Russia, Iran and Cuba are limited to defence ties.
III. Sanctions drastically limited Venezuela's oil exports to the US.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because the partnerships also cover energy and finance.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The US has treated the Caribbean as a critical zone of influence.
II. Sanctions drastically increased Venezuela's oil exports to the US.
III. Venezuela's economy suffered a drastic contraction, largely blamed on corruption, poor governance and overdependence on oil.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while statement II reverses the booklet's account of sanctions and exports.

questions.q: According to the booklet, gaining leverage over Venezuela's large oil reserves could help the US do what?
options: Reduce dependence on West Asian oil
questions.explanation: The booklet says such leverage could help the US diversify its energy sources and reduce dependence on West Asian oil.

questions.q: According to the booklet, which US President officially recognised Juan Guaido as Venezuela's legitimate leader?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that US President Donald Trump officially recognised Guaido as Venezuela's legitimate leader soon after his self-declaration.

quizzes.title: Sanctions and Strategic Interests
quizzes.passage: Venezuela lies on the northern coast of South America, bordered by Colombia, Brazil and Guyana. Venezuela's government and Washington have been locked in a dispute over the country's future. After Juan Guaido declared himself Acting President, tensions with Washington rose further. Caracas reacted sharply to these developments. The state-owned oil firm was placed under comprehensive sanctions, which have affected the country's ability to sell its crude. The sanctions were meant to pressure the government. Venezuela holds some of the largest oil reserves in the world, and so the dispute has a strong energy dimension. Venezuela has also built relationships with several governments outside the region, and Washington has watched these ties closely. Caracas has rejected the allegations made against it, arguing that they serve to justify a change of government. Caracas also says that migration and drug issues are being used as a cover for political goals. Venezuela's economy has suffered a drastic contraction in recent years, alongside high inflation and prolonged power outages. Shortages of food and problems in healthcare have added to the strain on ordinary citizens. Nicolas Maduro has led the government through these years, and critics have questioned the fairness of recent elections. Caracas and Washington give very different accounts of the dispute and its causes.

questions.q: After sanctions failed to dislodge the Maduro government, what type of measure did the US turn to? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the US turned to maritime interdictions aimed at choking Venezuela's oil-based revenues.

questions.q: Which Caribbean island nation is among Venezuela's partners? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Cuba among the states with which Venezuela has strengthened partnerships.

questions.q: With which country did Maduro sever diplomatic ties in retaliation? (two words)
questions.explanation: After Guaido's self-declaration, Maduro severed diplomatic ties with the United States and expelled American diplomats.

questions.q: What term describes the US approach that stresses hemispheric dominance? (one word, hyphenated form accepted)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes a Neo-Monroeist approach that emphasises hemispheric dominance.

questions.q: Which region did the US treat as a critical zone of influence, reminiscent of Cold War-era calculations? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Caribbean is increasingly treated as a critical zone of influence.

questions.q: Venezuela's partnerships with China, Russia and Iran span energy, defence and which third area? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Venezuela's partnerships cover energy cooperation, defence ties and financial arrangements.

questions.q: The US views Venezuela's alignments as a challenge to its strategic dominance in which hemisphere? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the US sees these alignments as a challenge to its strategic dominance in the Western Hemisphere.

quizzes.title: Monroe Doctrine and the UN
quizzes.passage: The Monroe Doctrine is one of the oldest foreign policy declarations of the United States. It was announced by an American president in the early nineteenth century, when European powers were looking to expand their presence in Latin America. The doctrine's early history is closely linked to the period after the Napoleonic wars. The policy rested on three core principles, which were set out when it was first proclaimed. Its first purpose was defensive, but the doctrine was later used to justify American intervention in the region. The Roosevelt Corollary of 1904 extended the doctrine, stating that the United States could act to keep stability in the Western Hemisphere. The United Nations was created to maintain international peace and security, yet it has very often struggled to stop unilateral military action by states. Some states have redefined the use of force as law enforcement or preventive self-defence. The Security Council is the body at the very centre of these efforts. Modern conflicts increasingly involve many hidden methods that blur the line between peace and war, and such conflicts are often described as gray-zone conflicts. Reform proposals have been put forward to make the Security Council more effective and more accountable.

questions.q: Which Monroe Doctrine principle states that European powers must not establish new colonies in the Americas?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists non-colonisation as a core principle, barring European powers from establishing new colonies in North or South America.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The UN Security Council has struggled to prevent unilateral military interventions.
Reason (R): P5 members can block any Security Council resolution.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet links the UN's difficulty in stopping interventions to the P5 members' power to block any resolution, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. NotPetya attack   ->   A. Cyberattack that disrupted global systems
II. Original aim of the Monroe Doctrine   ->   B. Stopping European re-colonisation of Latin America
III. Power of P5 members   ->   C. Can block any UN Security Council resolution
IV. Reform for gray-zone threats   ->   D. Binding gray-zone accountability protocol
questions.explanation: NotPetya is the cyberattack example, the doctrine originally aimed to stop European re-colonisation, P5 members can block resolutions, and the reform calls for a binding accountability protocol.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Regional organisations such as NATO, the AU and ECOWAS intervene without UN Security Council approval.
II. A veto override for mass atrocities is among the reform ideas discussed.
III. The Monroe Doctrine was originally designed to encourage European colonisation of Latin America.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II reflect the booklet, while statement III reverses the doctrine's original purpose of stopping European re-colonisation.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The UN faces unpaid regular dues from its members.
II. The P5 members are the US, Russia, China, UK and France.
III. The UN Security Council has no permanent members.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while statement III is false because the Council has five permanent members.

questions.q: Which set of tactics does the booklet list for modern gray-zone conflicts?
options: Cyberattacks, private military companies and proxies
questions.explanation: The booklet lists cyberattacks, PMCs and proxies as the tactics used in modern gray-zone conflicts.

questions.q: During the Cold War, the Monroe Doctrine was used for what purpose?
options: To expand European colonies in Africa
To counter Soviet influence in the Americas
To fund NATO expansion in Asia
questions.explanation: The booklet says the doctrine was used in the Cold War era to counter Soviet influence in the Americas.

quizzes.title: Monroe Doctrine and Multilateralism
quizzes.passage: The Monroe Doctrine is a policy that the United States announced in the early nineteenth century. It was meant to keep European powers from re-establishing colonies in Latin America, and the three core principles of the policy were stated at that time. Its first purpose was defensive, but later it was used to justify American military action in the region. The Roosevelt Corollary extended this idea, saying the United States could keep stability in the Western Hemisphere. The United Nations exists to maintain international peace and security, yet its work is often limited. Permanent members can block resolutions, and action frequently stalls when a major power is involved. The UN also faces funding problems, with unpaid dues and shortfalls for peacekeeping. Regional bodies have acted in crises without waiting for Security Council approval. Modern conflicts use hidden methods that blur the line between war and peace, and states have sometimes described military force as law enforcement. Reformers have suggested stronger accountability, limits on vetoes and public justification of decisions, and new rules for hybrid threats. Computer attacks, private contractors and proxies are among the tools used in these conflicts. Reform ideas also include a binding protocol for gray-zone threats and monitoring of cyber attacks.

questions.q: In which year did the NotPetya cyberattack disrupt global systems? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet cites the NotPetya cyberattack of 2017 as an example of a disruptive gray-zone attack.

questions.q: Which UN Charter article on the use of force do states bypass by redefining military force as law enforcement? (article number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says states bypass Article 2(4) by redefining military force as law enforcement or preventive self-defence.

questions.q: Which UN Charter article is cited for preventive self-defence? (article number)
questions.explanation: The booklet links preventive self-defence to Article 51 of the UN Charter.

questions.q: Which Monroe Doctrine principle bars European powers from interfering in the internal affairs of independent American states? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Europe should not interfere in the internal affairs of independent American states, which is the non-intervention principle.

questions.q: During the Cold War, the Monroe Doctrine was used to counter influence from which superpower? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the doctrine was used in the Cold War era to counter Soviet influence in the Americas.

questions.q: Which reform mechanism would let a P5 veto be set aside for mass atrocities? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet proposes a veto override mechanism for mass atrocities.

questions.q: Which regional organisation, besides NATO and the African Union, intervenes without Security Council approval? (one word)
accept: Economic Community of West African States
questions.explanation: The booklet names ECOWAS among the regional bodies that intervene without UNSC approval.
